title: Dentbird software designs dental crowns faster in university tests, and Ohio State researchers conclude that its designs need human review
summary: In university tests, Imagoworks' Dentbird software let technicians design crowns about four times faster, and Ohio State researchers concluded that its designs needed human review.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Dentbird uses deep learning and 3D dental data to detect margins and generate prosthesis designs. University researchers with no stated tie to Imagoworks tested Dentbird in 2025. Kanagawa Dental University researchers reported on 24 February 2025 that five technicians designed crowns about four times faster with Dentbird than with conventional computer-aided design (CAD) software. For one premolar crown, design time was 397.2 ± 80.4 minutes with the 3Shape Dental System and 99.4 ± 17.1 minutes with Dentbird. Ohio State researchers reported in April 2025 that six prosthodontists rated Dentbird single-crown designs as less acceptable than those of technicians and of a rival AI program. Imagoworks' submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, describes real-world pilots and automated design in minutes. It claims lower technician workload and shorter treatment workflows. The submission gives no standardized before-and-after timing comparison and no patient health outcomes. The authors of a clinical study published in August 2025, funded by the Korea Medical Device Development Fund, found that Dentbird crowns fitted 62 patients about as well as conventional crowns, with larger lingual and occlusal discrepancies. In December 2025 the Ohio State researchers found that Dentbird saved design time on 30 bridges but underperformed on esthetic and functional criteria. They concluded that the designs needed human review.
purpose: Automate dental prosthesis design and reduce manual CAD work.

ratings.reason: Researchers at Kanagawa Dental University and Ohio State University measured shorter design time with Dentbird. Their tests took place in laboratories, and the authors did not measure workload in a dental lab's routine work.
The authors of a clinical study found that Dentbird crowns fitted about as well as conventional crowns, which shows no gain for patients over the usual method.

ai_role.statement: Researchers isolated the software's part in controlled comparisons. At Kanagawa Dental University, the same technicians designed crowns with Dentbird and with conventional CAD, and design time fell when Dentbird detected the margins and generated the crown automatically. At Ohio State, prosthodontists rated unedited Dentbird designs below those of technicians, so people still review and correct the output.

evidence.citation: Sawangsri K, Bekkali M, Hsieh YL, et al., Acceptability, deviation, and efficiency of 2 fully automated CAD software programs in designing 3-unit fixed dental prostheses: A comparative study, Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry, 5 December 2025. Ohio State University authors with no stated tie to either vendor; they found that Dentbird saved design time on 30 bridges but underperformed on esthetic and functional criteria.
evidence.title: Acceptability, deviation, and efficiency of 2 fully automated CAD software programs in designing 3-unit fixed dental prostheses: A comparative study
evidence.quote: Although both systems improved design efficiency, human oversight remains essential for occlusal and proximal contact, connector design, and anterior FDPs.

fields.summary: In university tests, Imagoworks' Dentbird software let technicians design crowns about four times faster, and Ohio State researchers concluded that its designs needed human review.
fields.account: Dentbird uses deep learning and 3D dental data to detect margins and generate prosthesis designs. University researchers with no stated tie to Imagoworks tested Dentbird in 2025. Kanagawa Dental University researchers reported on 24 February 2025 that five technicians designed crowns about four times faster with Dentbird than with conventional computer-aided design (CAD) software. For one premolar crown, design time was 397.2 ± 80.4 minutes with the 3Shape Dental System and 99.4 ± 17.1 minutes with Dentbird. Ohio State researchers reported in April 2025 that six prosthodontists rated Dentbird single-crown designs as less acceptable than those of technicians and of a rival AI program. Imagoworks' submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, describes real-world pilots and automated design in minutes. It claims lower technician workload and shorter treatment workflows. The submission gives no standardized before-and-after timing comparison and no patient health outcomes. The authors of a clinical study published in August 2025, funded by the Korea Medical Device Development Fund, found that Dentbird crowns fitted 62 patients about as well as conventional crowns, with larger lingual and occlusal discrepancies. In December 2025 the Ohio State researchers found that Dentbird saved design time on 30 bridges but underperformed on esthetic and functional criteria. They concluded that the designs needed human review.
